definition: An attack in which an adversary queries a deployed model repeatedly to reconstruct a functionally similar copy of it.
details: Model extraction attacks threaten the intellectual property and security of proprietary models served via APIs, motivating rate limiting and query monitoring as defenses.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. Think of it this way: An attack in which an adversary queries a deployed model repeatedly to reconstruct a functionally similar copy of it. And here is the clever part: Model extraction attacks threaten the intellectual property and security of proprietary models served via APIs, motivating rate limiting and query monitoring as defenses. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” And that is Model Extraction Attack — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.
